data.headline: Germie Bernard And Bhayshul Tuten Prove The Wire Still Has Juice
data.deck: Week 6 waiver darlings go off while half the league starts the wrong running back
body: Adam's First Down Syndrome didn't win with Derrick Henry, who No. 22'd his way to 5 points on 17 carries. He won because Germie Bernard, a flex spot filler who was projected for 9.96, caught 11 of 12 targets for 87 yards and a touchdown and dropped 25.7 points on a Victorious Secrets team that never had a chance. That's the whole blueprint for this league right now: stop waiting on your studs and start trusting whoever is actually getting the ball. Jaxon Smith-Njigba chipped in 25.4 of his own, which means Adam started two guys for a combined near-51 points while Taylor was out here starting Brandin Cooks for 2.3.

Bearcat's Hog Tied and Deep Fried lost by 57.1 to Jackson's juggernaut, which is its own tragedy, but buried in that disaster is Bhayshul Tuten going for 24.7 on 12 carries and 4 catches with 2 receiving touchdowns, nearly doubling his 13.19 projection. That's a legitimate RB2 streaming option humming along on a 1-6 team, which is the fantasy equivalent of finding a Ferrari key in a couch at a house that's on fire.

Meanwhile Matt's Shough Her Gently continues to find new ways to self-sabotage. He benched Tre Tucker, who put up 26.7, in favor of Tyler Allgeier's 5.8, a decision that cost him 20.9 points in a game he lost by 12.06. Cam Skattebo also scored a flat zero in his lineup. Matt is now L4 and sitting at 1-6, and at some point you have to wonder if the waiver wire is working against him on purpose.

data.headline: Taylor Does It Again, Victorious Secrets Hits Rock Bottom Twice
data.deck: 63.58 points, a 53.56 point beatdown, and a second career Shart for Taylor's dumpster fire of a roster.
body: Let's start with the number because the number deserves its own eulogy. 63.58. That's what Taylor's Victorious Secrets put up in Week 6, and it is not a typo, it is not a rough week, it is a full systems failure from top to bottom of the lineup. Adam's First Down Syndrome strolled in and dropped 117.14 on him, a 53.56 point margin that isn't a loss so much as a public records request. Taylor fell to 1-6. His weekRank for the week was 14th. Out of everyone. Dead last.

Let's talk about the actual humans responsible for this. Bo Nix went for 4.48 points against a projection of 13.36, good for an 8.88 point no show, throwing for 107 yards on 17 of 27 with 4 carries for 2 yards, the statistical profile of a man who forgot the game was happening. Kyren Williams, the worst starter on the roster by the numbers, managed 9.7 points on 10 carries for 50 yards and 3 of 6 for 17 yards through the air, nearly 11.17 points under what he was supposed to deliver. Brandin Cooks caught 1 of 2 targets for 13 yards and 2.3 points. Isaiah Williams rushed once for 4 yards and 0.4 points. Terry McLaurin, a start over actual production, caught his lone target for 27 yards and all of 3.7 points, a brutal 7.9 points under projection. The Jacksonville Jaguars defense finished at negative 2 points after allowing an interception and surrendering 34 points themselves, a 10.04 point disaster relative to what Taylor needed from them. The lone bright spot was Kyle Pitts Sr., who hauled in 5 of 7 for 60 yards and 2 touchdowns for 23 points, 15.44 points over projection, but one man carrying a corpse up a hill doesn't change what's waiting at the top.

Here's the part that should really keep Taylor up at night. He benched J.K. Dobbins, who scored 13.6 points, in favor of Terry McLaurin's 3.7, a 9.9 point gift he handed back to the universe for no reason at all. Then, because apparently one unforced error wasn't enough, he benched the Cincinnati Bengals defense, who scored a modest 0, in favor of the Jacksonville Jaguars, who scored negative 2, flushing away another 2 points on a defensive swap that had no business happening. Stack those decisions next to a 53.56 point loss and you start to understand that this wasn't bad luck. This was a man building his own coffin and then personally nailing the lid.

And this isn't Taylor's first rodeo at the bottom. He sharted in Week 1 too, 63.04 points back then, and now he's got two Sharts to his name on the season, a club nobody wants a loyalty card for. His power ranking actually ticked up two spots this week, which tells you everything about how bad everyone below him is doing, because his playoff odds still sit at a bleak 0.2 percent. Victorious Secrets by name, catastrophe by nature, and at 1-6 with 9 weeks remaining, there is a lot more losing left to budget for.

So here it is, the whole wretched communion, bigger than the pitchers, bigger than the hose, bigger than the twelve pack in the parking lot, bigger even than the kiddie pool baptism, because two Sharts in six weeks means baptism isn't enough anymore, Taylor needs full immersion. Drain the actual pool. The real one, in-ground, deep end and all. Empty every bottle in the house into it, every pitcher, every can with the lying cartoon animal, every last drop, and submerge him fully, face down, until the number 63.58 dissolves off his skin like it's trying to escape too. He comes up only when someone confirms in writing that his playoff odds have moved off 0.2. Chug, bitch.
data.signOff: So here it is, the whole wretched communion, bigger than the pitchers, bigger than the hose, bigger than the twelve pack in the parking lot, bigger even than the kiddie pool baptism, because two Sharts in six weeks means baptism isn't enough anymore, Taylor needs full immersion. Drain the actual pool. The real one, in-ground, deep end and all. Empty every bottle in the house into it, every pitcher, every can with the lying cartoon animal, every last drop, and submerge him fully, face down, until the number 63.58 dissolves off his skin like it's trying to escape too. He comes up only when someone confirms in writing that his playoff odds have moved off 0.2. Chug, bitch.

data.headline: The Trade Desk Is Open And Everyone Stayed Home
data.deck: Zero trades got done in Week 6, so instead we are grading the real deals that got made at the worst possible time: starting lineups.
body: Let the record show the Squirtnite FFL trade desk processed exactly nothing this week. No picks moved, no bye week panic deals, not even a courtesy throw-in. While you all sat on your hands, your benches were out here making trades for you, and most of you lost the deal.

Andrew traded Bryce Young for Aaron Rodgers before the games even started and it cost him 3.82 points. Rodgers went 16.02, Young sat there with 19.84, and Bibi's Ballers 69 lost by 6.9 with 109.82 on the board, the single highest losing score of the week. Grade: F for the swap, A for the heartbreak tour.

Trip somehow benched Trevor Lawrence's 27.34 to start Matthew Stafford's 16.88, a 10.46 point self-inflicted wound, and 50 Shades of Zay got run off the field by 26.6 anyway with a week rank of 11. That is not a trade, that is a hostage situation.

Two men cost themselves the whole game. Matt sat Tre Tucker's 26.7 for Tyler Allgeier's 5.8, a 20.9 point gift to Burrowed Alive in a 12.06 point loss, textbook benched the win. John did the same thing smaller, parking Blake Corum's 14 for Bijan Robinson's 7.3, a 6.7 point cost in a 6.14 point loss to Cook'd. Every trade on the books this week gets an Incomplete, because the only transactions anyone made were with their own Sunday morning lineup, and the house always wins.

data.headline: The Hardware: Week 6 Banquet Of Shame And Glory
data.deck: Seven trophies, zero dignity. Grab a napkin, Taylor still owes a chug.
body: Pull up a folding chair, pour something cheap, and let's hand out the hardware nobody asked to win. Week 6 gave us a legitimate blowout, a legitimate heartbreak, and at least two bench decisions that should get a man's Sleeper account confiscated. On with the ceremony.

Manager of the Week goes to Jackson of Ha Ha Ha, Now Heres A Guy, who dropped 130.40 points and didn't even need his whole roster to do it. D'Andre Swift popped for 23 points against a 15.13 projection, George Kittle chipped in 17.9, and Jackson still had enough juice left over to leave points rotting on the bench, which we will absolutely get back to.
The Shart belongs to Taylor of Victorious Secrets, who mustered 63.58 points and got run over by Adam's First Down Syndrome. We already spent our good jokes on him up top. Chug up, Taylor.

Blowout honors go to Jackson again, because apparently one trophy case wasn't enough this week. Ha Ha Ha, Now Heres A Guy buried bearcat2789's Hog tied and deep fried by 57.10 points, even with Bhayshul Tuten going off for 24.7 against a 13.19 projection on the other side. Didn't matter. Wasn't close.

Squeaker goes to Jack of Cook'd, who escaped BedBathNBIJAN22 by 6.14 points in what doubled as the Game of the Week. John's Bijan Robinson no showed with 7.3 points against a 25.16 projection, and John still benched Blake Corum's 14 points to start him, a 6.7 point gift that's bigger than the margin he lost by. That's not bad luck, John, that's a self inflicted wound.

Lucky Dog belongs to Sean of Burrowed Alive, who won with just 102.78 points over Matt's Shough Her Gently. Matt's Cam Skattebo delivered a flat 0 against a 10.15 projection, and Matt still benched Tre Tucker's 26.7 points to roll with Tyler Allgeier's 5.8, a 20.9 point gift to the football gods. Matt is now L4. The vibes are not improving.

Heartbreaker goes to Andrew of Bibi's Ballers 69, who lost with 109.82 points to Ben's Jackson Off in a game decided by 6.9. Andrew also benched Bryce Young's 19.84 points for Aaron Rodgers' 16.02, a 3.82 point cost that stings a lot more in a loss this tight.

Bench Rot, fittingly, goes right back to Jackson, who left 52.96 points on his own bench and still won by 57.10 and posted the week's best score. He sat Tyler Shough's 26.96 for Jayden Daniels' 21, a 5.96 point cost, and swapped the Jets' 6 points for the Niners' 5, giving up another point for fun. Some men just have too much roster. Ceremony adjourned, see you next week.

data.headline: Big Performances: Josef Doubles Up While Trip Torches His Own Bench
data.deck: Six guys went off this week. Only some of their managers were smart enough to notice before kickoff.
body: Josef had the best fantasy day anybody had all week and split it between two guys on the same roster. Christian McCaffrey went for 16 CAR, 64 YD, 2 RUSH TD, 9/10 REC, 53 YD, 1 FUM, good for 30.7 against a projection of 20.56, a plus 10.14 beatdown of Vegas math. Then Malik Nabers casually dropped 12/15 REC, 165 YD for 28.5 points on a 14.94 projection, a plus 13.56 that should be illegal in a league this size. Zyn-bo Squisher rolled in at 4-2 on a W1 streak and buried 50 Shades of Zay 121.38 to 94.78, a 26.6 margin that was never in doubt.

Which brings us to Trip, who had the single best individual stat line of anyone not named McCaffrey or Nabers and still lost. Kenneth Walker III went 19 CAR, 128 YD, 2 RUSH TD, 2/3 REC, 11 YD for 27.9 points on a 22.76 projection, a plus 5.14 night. Didn't matter. Trip benched Trevor Lawrence, who put up 27.34 points, in favor of Matthew Stafford's 16.88, a 10.46 point gift he handed to Josef for free. Then he doubled down and sat Emmett Johnson's 4.4 points for Juwan Johnson's zero, another 4.4 down the drain. Harold Fannin Jr. finished with 1.9 on an 11.18 projection too, just to make sure nothing worked. Trip entered the week 4-2 on an L2 skid and his weekRank of 11 tells the whole ugly story.

Adam ran the same two-star trick on First Down Syndrome. Germie Bernard caught 11/12 REC, 87 YD, 1 REC TD for 25.7 on a 9.96 projection, a plus 15.74 explosion, while Jaxon Smith-Njigba added 12/16 REC, 134 YD for 25.4 against a 22.5 projection. First Down Syndrome demolished Victorious Secrets 117.14 to 63.58, a 53.56 margin, entering the week 3-3 on a W2 run.

And then there's Bearcat, who got a legitimately great game from Bhayshul Tuten, 12 CAR, 39 YD, 4/4 REC, 48 YD, 2 REC TD for 24.7 on a 13.19 projection, and it still bought him nothing. Hog tied and deep fried lost to Ha Ha Ha, Now Heres A Guy 73.3 to 130.4, a 57.1 margin, dropping Bearcat to 1-5 on an L4 streak that Tuten alone could not fix.

data.headline: Jackson Wins Manager Of The Week, Immediately Gets Humbled By His Own Bench
data.deck: Ha Ha Ha, Now Heres A Guy drops 130.40 on a corpse, and somehow that is still the softest Manager of the Week line all season.
body: Jackson's Ha Ha Ha, Now Heres A Guy put up 130.40 this week and ran his record to 6-1, flattening Bearcat's Hog tied and deep fried by 57.10, the biggest margin in the league this week. Bearcat came in on an L4 skid and left on one, and honestly this matchup was dead the moment the lineups locked. Jackson's weekRank of 1 says it all. He didn't just win, he won like a guy who knew the other side of the bracket forgot to show up.

The engine here was D'Andre Swift out of the flex, who went for 23 points on 16 carries for 44 yards and two rushing touchdowns plus four catches for 26 yards, beating his 15.13 projection by a wide margin. Jayden Daniels backed him up with 21 points on 29 of 40 for 300 yards and two touchdowns, clearing his 17.35 projection, and George Kittle chipped in 17.9 points on a 5 for 8, 69 yard, one touchdown day that also cleared his number. That's three starters outperforming their projections in the same lineup, which is how you get to 130.40 against a team that had no business being on the same field.

Now the part where we remember Jackson is still a degenerate who got bailed out by the schedule. He benched Tyler Shough, who put up 26.96 points, in favor of Jayden Daniels, who scored 21, leaving 5.96 points sitting on the table, and he also sat the Jets defense's 6 points for the Niners' 5, another point gone for nothing. Add it up and Jackson left 52.96 points on his own bench this week, the most in the league, and somehow still cruised. Puka Nacua caught six balls for 80 yards and still landed at 14 points against a 22.63 projection, a legit bust in a winning lineup nobody noticed because Bearcat's side of the ledger was a crime scene. And for a little perspective: Jackson's own 130.40 projected out to 138.51 before kickoff, meaning the Manager of the Week actually scored under his own number. Compare that to the other weekly highs on record this season, 169.86, 136.88, 151.64, 154.78 and 174.86, and this is the softest winning score to wear the crown all year. Enjoy the trophy, Jackson. It's heavy, but it's hollow.
data.signOff: That's the paper. See you on the waiver wire, degenerates.

data.headline: Jack Survives A Bijan Implosion To Keep Cook'd Rolling
data.deck: The tightest margin of the week came down to one bench decision that cost John more than the final score ever did.
body: Game of the Week honors go to the only matchup that finished inside a single score, and it delivered exactly the kind of gut punch this league exists for. Jack's Cook'd squad escaped with a 112 to 105.86 win over John's BedBathNBIJAN22, a margin of 6.14 that was the smallest of the entire week. Jack improves to 5-1 and extends his win streak to W5. John falls to 2-4 on a L3 skid that is starting to look like a pattern instead of a rough patch.

Jack did it with Michael Penix Jr. lighting up the box score at 23.1 points against a 13.62 projection, going 19 of 33 for 225 yards and 3 touchdowns despite a fumble. James Cook III matched the vibe with 24.3 points on 22 carries for 95 yards and a touchdown, adding three catches for 58 yards out of the backfield. Colston Loveland was the flex that nobody saw coming, posting 18.5 points on a 65 yard, one touchdown day against a projection of just 9.46. Not everything clicked. Nick Folk was a non factor at kicker, scoring 1 point against an 8.24 projection, but it did not matter with that much firepower around him.

John actually had the better individual story on paper. DeVonta Smith was his best starter by a mile, hauling in 7 of 14 targets for 75 yards and a touchdown for 20.5 points against an 11.9 projection. But the game turned on Bijan Robinson, who was projected for 25.16 points and delivered 7.3, a brutal 9 carries for 61 yards, 2 catches that went for negative 8 yards, nowhere close to the workhorse number John needed. That bust alone buried the upside John's 133.9 projected total promised, and he finished well under it at 105.86 while Jack cleared his 95.23 projection with room to spare.

Here is the part that will keep John up at night. He had Blake Corum sitting on his bench with 14 points, and started Bijan Robinson instead, a decision that cost him 6.7 points. The final margin was 6.14. Run that math in your head as many times as you want, the swap alone would have flipped the result. John's bench finished with 24.7 points on the sideline doing nothing while his starting running back no showed the game plan.

It was not even the worst bench call of the week, which tells you how deep the misery runs in this league right now. Over in the Burrowed Alive versus Shough Her Gently game, Matt benched Tre Tucker and his 26.7 points in favor of Tyler Allgeier's 5.8, a decision that cost him 20.9 points in a game he lost by 12.06. Matt's error was bigger in raw numbers, but Jack and John's game is the one where the bench call and the final margin lined up close enough to make every John supporter want to throw a remote. Jack's Cook'd ranked 5th in scoring this week while John's squad came in 8th, and the gap between those two numbers was exactly as thin as it felt watching it live.

data.headline: Bench Mistakes Did More Damage Than Any Defense in Week 6
data.deck: Andrew and Trip and John and Jeff all found creative ways to beat themselves, Taylor found the bottom of the barrel, and Jackson just kept doing whatever he wants.
body: Six weeks in and the real villain in Squirtnite is still every manager's own roster. This week it was lineup cards doing the damage, not corners and linebackers, and there's a lot of self inflicted stuff to get through.

Ben's Jackson Off needed every bit of 116.72 to hold off Andrew's Bibi's Ballers 69 at 109.82, a 6.9 point margin that stayed sweaty to the final whistle. Andrew helped make it close against himself too, starting Aaron Rodgers for 16.02 while Bryce Young sat on his bench with 19.84, a 3.82 point gift he didn't need to give. Jacoby Brissett nearly blew it for Ben anyway, going 6.92 against a 13.4 projection, but Matthew Golden's 22.4 bailed him out.

Josef's Zyn-bo Squisher flattened Trip's 50 Shades of Zay, 121.38 to 94.78, a 26.6 point gap that Trip widened all by himself. He benched Trevor Lawrence's 27.34 to start Matthew Stafford's 16.88, a 10.46 point cost, then doubled down starting Juwan Johnson over Emmett Johnson, Juwan finishing with a goose egg and burning another 4.4. Meanwhile Josef just sat back and watched Christian McCaffrey go for 30.7 and Malik Nabers torch the Giants secondary for 28.5.

Sean's Burrowed Alive beat Matt's Shough Her Gently, 102.78 to 90.72, and Matt handed him the margin and then some. Tre Tucker sat on Matt's bench for 26.7 points while Tyler Allgeier started and managed 5.8, a 20.9 point gift that officially counts as benching the win. Cam Skattebo didn't even bother showing up, a zero against a 10.15 projection, stretching Matt's skid to L4.

Adam's First Down Syndrome put up 117.14 and buried Taylor's Victorious Secrets at 63.58, a 53.56 point wipeout that locked in this week's Shart. Germie Bernard was the engine, 25.7 points against a 9.96 projection, while Derrick Henry no showed for Adam with 5 points on a 17.88 projection and it still didn't matter. Taylor got a flash of hope from Kyle Pitts going for 23 against a 7.56 projection, but Bo Nix at 4.48 and Kyren Williams stuck at 9.7 against a 20.87 projection buried it fast.

Jack's Cook'd survived the Game of the Week against John's BedBathNBIJAN22, winning 112 to 105.86 by a Squeaker margin of 6.14. John's Bijan Robinson no showed when it mattered most, 7.3 points against a 25.16 projection, and John still benched Blake Corum's 14 points to start him anyway. Michael Penix Jr. torched John's defense for 23.1 against a 13.62 projection to get Jack over the top.

Jackson's Ha Ha Ha, Now Heres A Guy ran up 130.4 on Bearcat's Hog tied and deep fried at 73.3, the week's Blowout at 57.1. Bhayshul Tuten went off for Bearcat anyway, 24.7 against a 13.19 projection, completely wasted in a loss. Jackson left 52.96 points on his own bench, benching Tyler Shough's 26.96 to start Jayden Daniels' 21, and didn't even need to sweat it with D'Andre Swift going for 23 and George Kittle adding 17.9.

Aaron's Romo911 took down Jeff's Chase Browns with Downs, 107.6 to 95.02, a 12.58 point final behind Isaiah Likely erupting for 23.9 against a 13.72 projection. Jeff's Dak Prescott had a rough one, 11.02 points against an 18.89 projection, and Jeff made it worse benching the Cleveland Browns defense's 11 points to start the Indianapolis Colts, who gave him 5.
